conclusion.question: can the Gamma-guided allocation be claimed to beat the uniform allocation?
conclusion.answer: no (bounded: not beaten at the capacity-matched setting, and not equated either -- the difference is resolvable in the opposite direction)
conclusion.headline: Under the capacity-matched design the Gamma-guided allocation does not beat the uniform allocation; it is significantly worse. The paired seed-level difference is -3570.1 [-5524.2, -1850.3] (95% percentile bootstrap, 6 pairs, all 6 per-seed differences negative), and no resample of the paired differences reaches zero. Equivalence is also rejected: at a margin of one uniform sample sd (1900) the paired TOST gives p = 0.916, and TOST would not pass until the margin reached 6232, so the arms are not equivalent -- they are separated, in the direction opposite to the claim. The unpaired Welch test on the same six seed pairs gives p = 0.0055, which is the digit the manuscript prints.

caveats_that_must_survive: the capacity-matched comparison rests on 6 seeds per arm; the percentile CI is over those seeds
the matched-loss comparison rests on n = 2 seeds per arm; its CI is the seed spread, not a 5% false-positive guarantee
the equivalence margin is data-derived (one sample sd of the uniform arm), not pre-registered; the equivalence statement is conditional on that margin and the smallest equivalent margin is 6232
the random pool is ten plans; four further random draws were excluded because they duplicate rule solutions
the 1e-3 sweep and the matched-loss control have two seeds per arm
the manuscript's printed +1478 is a rounding artefact of 1477.4502, which rounds to +1477
not_claimed: no claim that the Gamma-guided allocation improves alignment energy over uniform
no claim about which allocation is better in general; the reversal under matched loss and the underpowered random-pool comparison are both reported rather than resolved
no claim that the two arms are equivalent: equivalence is rejected at one uniform sample sd
